narrative.text: The statement from the Lytheiran intermediary is brief. The small currency hedge you placed — 1,000 ₭, not the full 4,000 ₭ that was offered — has reached its settlement date. You told yourself at the time that this was not speculation. It was insurance. A hedge against uncertainty. A prudent household protecting itself against the possibility that the Krone would decline despite your best efforts to stabilize it. The settlement will tell you whether that argument holds — or whether it was always a distinction without a difference.

One thousand ₭. Not the full position — not the bet that would have made me wealthy from my country's decline. I told myself that the scale mattered: that hedging was different from speculating, that protecting my family was different from betting against my country. The distinction is real, but it is thin. The 1,000 ₭ position is still a short against the Krone. It is still routed through a foreign intermediary. It still means I had a personal financial stake in whether my own economic policies succeeded or failed. The only question is whether the stake was small enough to be defensible — or whether the very fact of the stake makes it indefensible.

choices.text: "The hedge paid out — 5,000 ₭. A modest return on a modest position. The Krone declined, and the hedge did what hedges are supposed to do: it cushioned the blow. I did not cause the decline. I did not benefit from it in any way that matters compared to what the country lost. But I protected my family, which is what I said I was doing. I will take the return. I will not apologize for being prudent. And I will remind anyone who asks that I invested one thousand ₭, not four thousand — because even when I was hedging, I was hedging responsibly. The difference between insurance and speculation is scale. I kept the scale small. That matters."

"The hedge did not pay out. The Krone stabilized, the position closed at a loss, and the 1,000 ₭ is gone. Good. I am relieved — not about losing the money, but about what losing it means. It means the economy did not crash. It means my policies worked. It means I can honestly say that the 1,000 ₭ I lost was a small price to pay for the country's stability. If anyone ever asks about the hedge, I will tell them exactly that: I bet against the Krone as insurance, the Krone held, and I lost the bet. That is a story about a Chancellor whose policy succeeded and whose hedge failed. It is the right outcome, in the right order."
